replacements.new:
than left ownerless.
A new global task is filed under its creator lane's project (the lane's
project membership, when it still belongs to the pane's running
process); a lane with no membership takes the `--parent` task's project
when it could have named that project itself. `--project NAME` files it
under a named project instead: your own, or one you hold a planner grant
for (the owner may name any; any other name is refused). `--no-project`
files it under none. A lane with global membership files unmapped tasks
unless it names a project.
A task that waits for something is BLOCKED with what it waits for, so
the next-job handoff skips it: `task block <id> --waiting-on owner |
evidence | release | numbers | task:<id> | pr:<repo>#<number>`
(`--reason` adds the detail). The kind is shown in `task read`,
`task list`, `task backlog` and `task_metrics`. `task:<id>` reopens
the task when that task completes, and `pr:<repo>#<number>` when
review-sync sees that pull request merged (if it closes without
merging the task stays blocked and gets a note). Every other wait is
cleared with `task unblock`.

replacements.new:
`dunk-poll` is a small native client: one socket request returns status +
inbox count + unread messages + dunks (optionally panes/tasks). By default
the answer is compact: only the dunks that target the caller's pane (a
dunk records its target, not who created it), each without the text it
types, and `--tasks` rows reduced to id, status,
priority, scope, assignees and title. `--all` lists every dunk in the
fleet (still without text); `--full` returns everything the daemon sent.
A caller that shows the fleet's dunks (a sidebar, a status board) must
pass `--all`. It
replaces three full CLI startups per sidebar poll (the owner's CPU note)

replacements.old:
Since 2.70.32 a batch is marked read only after the result is built, so a
read that fails no longer consumes the mail. A REPEATED batch after an error
is the fix working, not a bug: the same messages are offered again until a
read completes. `--peek` still marks nothing at all.
replacements.new:
A read prepares the complete response before atomically committing its read
marks and recovery receipt. A preparation or receipt-write failure leaves
the batch unread. A repeated batch after an error is safe redelivery, not
a new message. `--peek` still changes neither mail nor the recovery receipt.

replacements.old:
Recover follows the read rule, not the ack rule: like inbox read it is
permissive (inspecting a stranded mailbox is how the backlog gets drained),
while ack stays scoped to the caller's own mailbox.
replacements.new:
Recover and ack use the same mailbox authorization as read. Every role
that can read inbox mail, including planners, can recover and acknowledge
its own messages. Ordinary lanes cannot recover another lane's or the
human owner's mailbox. Existing privileged read access is unchanged.
Only acknowledge IDs whose bodies you actually received and displayed; if
a read response is missing its bodies, recover first instead of acknowledging.
Empty reads preserve the last non-empty receipt. Recovery may be repeated
after another lost response; explicit acknowledgment clears only the
acknowledged mail from the receipt. Normal reads still mark read without
acknowledging, and the messages-only default remains unchanged.
